intended_object: The type of functions that give a `Decidable` instance for every relation symbol of `L` evaluated at every tuple in the structure `M`, i.e. "every relation of the structure has a decision procedure". The name, the body and its single use (a classical instance at line 80) all point to this.
explanation: This is Lean data used to drive typeclass inference. For each relation symbol `r` of arity `k` and each tuple `v : Fin k → M`, it supplies an element of Lean's `Decidable (s.rel r v)`. In classical mathematics every proposition is decidable in this sense: the library's only use (line 80) fills it in with `Classical.dec`. So it does not pick out any class of structures. It is an implementation device that lets `if`/`decide` work on relation evaluations. It is not a notion such as "a computable structure" or "a structure with decidable atomic diagram", because nothing here asks the decision procedure to be computable in any mathematical sense. It therefore has no standard mathematical counterpart.
